question: Should experimental OpenClaw Claw packages adopt `CLAW.md` YAML frontmatter as the canonical exported manifest while continuing to accept the existing JSON representation?
rationale: The mechanics are testable, but choosing the canonical human-authored and exported package format creates a lasting product and compatibility contract that automation cannot approve.

options.title: Approve after RFC review
options.body: Adopt `CLAW.md` after the RFC and dependency stack are approved, while preserving JSON reads and explicit compatibility coverage.

options.title: Keep JSON canonical
options.body: Accept Markdown only as an optional input format and continue exporting `openclaw.claw.json` until a later specification decision.

options.title: Defer the format
options.body: Pause this slice until the harness-agnostic Claw specification determines the shared manifest representation.

recommendation.title: Approve after RFC review
recommendation.body: Adopt `CLAW.md` after the RFC and dependency stack are approved, while preserving JSON reads and explicit compatibility coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: They were explicitly routed into the discussion and are the strongest available owner for the product-level format decision rather than implementation follow-up.
